title: Did temporary foreign workers hold down Canadian wages?

hook.question: Did temporary foreign workers hold down wages?

yearSub: Average hourly wage, adjusted for inflation to 2025 dollars
between: Between cards, the year counts up and each line extends to that year's inflation-adjusted average hourly wage; dashed lines mark Temporary Foreign Worker Program changes; bars below (separate scale) show TFWP permit holders on December 31.

plan.line: real wage growth as TFW permits went from 29,220 to 93,745
after the cap; permits fell to 46,050 by 2017. Minimum wages also rose, so this alone can’t prove why
TFWP permit holders on Dec. 31, the most since at least 2000. Food & hotel wages 2019–2025: +0.8%/yr

summary.kicker: Did it hold wages down? One study’s answer: a little
summary.line: more pay for Canadians in low-wage jobs that used TFWs after the 2014 limits, compared with similar jobs the limits didn’t touch
summary.sub: Rough guide: on the 2014 food & hotel average of $18.30/hr (2025 dollars), that’s about 68–82¢ an hour. Study: Chen & Fang, Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies, 2025.

note: Source: Statistics Canada, tables 14-10-0064-01 (average hourly wage, all employees 15+) and 18-10-0005-01 (CPI, to 2025 dollars); IRCC open data, TFWP permit holders on Dec. 31 (preliminary; 2025 not yet published). Program dates: Government of Canada (July 2002 low-skill pilot; June 20, 2014 overhaul; Sept 26, 2024 changes). Averages change when the mix of workers changes. Lines grow between years as animation.
references: Chen, W.-H. & Fang, T. (2025). Restricting temporary foreign labour: evidence on wage effects from Canada's 2014 policy reform. Journal of Ethnic and Migration Studies. IZA DP 18240: https://www.iza.org/publications/dp18240
IRCC Operational Bulletin 113 (2009): July 2002 Pilot Project for Occupations Requiring Lower Levels of Formal Training
ESDC news release, June 20, 2014: Government of Canada overhauls the Temporary Foreign Worker Program
ESDC Question Period Note EWDOL_Dec2024_017: tightening measures effective September 26, 2024
Champagne, J. (2025). The Shift in Canadian Immigration Composition and its Effect on Wages. Bank of Canada Staff Discussion Paper 2025-8
method: Average hourly wages (current dollars) multiplied by CPI(2025)/CPI(year). Growth rates are compound annual rates between the named years. The chart is descriptive; the causal estimate is quoted from the cited difference-in-differences study, not computed here.
